name: Down to Nothing
label: Revelation
lede: David Wood and Daniel Spector, friends since age five, started a straight edge band in Richmond, wrote a record that sends fans to Belle Isle, and kept it going while Wood played bass for Terror almost 300 days a year.

eras.title: Fights at the door, fireworks in Sheffield
eras.text: Down to Nothing came out of the Guerrilla Crew, a straight edge collective of Richmond teenagers, at a time when Spector says a late-90s show guaranteed "at least one or two" fights. They played Twisters on Grace Street, put out records on Dead By 23 and Thorp, and took their first UK tour in 2005.

years.h: Two friends since age five start a band at Twisters
years.p: Wood and Spector, both in high school, add guitarist Alan Long. The first show, possibly under the name Detonation, is at Twisters with Shut Down and From Earth to Ashes.
years.xp:
Wood told Dying Scene he'd started experimenting with drugs at about twelve, before hardcore pulled him to straight edge: "None of us were straight-edge before we got into hardcore."

Twisters, 929 Grace Street, later became Strange Matter. Spector and guitarist Ryan "Groater" Groat split the riff-writing early on, and Hunter Jennings took over after Groat left.

years.h: A Dead By 23 7" lands when Wood is eighteen
years.p: The band's first release is on Dead By 23 Records around 2002. Wood tells DxR he was 18 then.

years.h: First full-length, Save It for the Birds, on Thorp
years.p: Down to Nothing's debut album comes out on Thorp Records, the label that also puts out their second.

years.h: Alan Long can't tour, so a Daytona bassist gets the call
years.p: Down to Nothing meet Jared Carman's band in Daytona and recruit him on bass for the 2005 tour. Carman later also plays in [[Trapped Under Ice|94c44a31-3f7b-4c5d-aa54-2bf47eeac5d5]].
years.xp: Wood told Dying Scene that Carman was brought in during 2005 because Long couldn't tour. The band had met his group while passing through Florida.

years.h: Eleven songs in under 21 minutes on Splitting Headache
years.p: Thorp Records, July 12. It opens on Go Ahead wit Yo' Fake Ass and closes on I'm So Lucky.
play: Go Ahead wit Yo' Fake Ass

years.cap: Stage dive during a Down to Nothing set, summer 2005
years.h: Fireworks on Guy Fawkes Night in Sheffield
years.p: On their first UK tour, with On Thin Ice, the band play Sheffield on November 5. Wood says they "bought heaps of fireworks and ran a muck all night being bad little boys."
years.xp:
Wood tells DxR it was fall 2005 and Guy Fawkes night fell on a show date.

The Cardiff set filmed at Dempseys comes from the same tour era; the uploader dates it 2005, the title says 2006.

eras.title: Revelation signs the Richmond kids
eras.text: Revelation, home of Judge and Gorilla Biscuits, put out three Down to Nothing records in three years, one with a guest spot from Have Heart's Patrick Flynn. Then Terror offered Wood a job.

years.cap: Down to Nothing at the Log Cabin, Toms River, New Jersey, July 7, 2006
years.h: Higher Learning 7" is the first record for Revelation
years.p: REV 140. The first pressing is 104 purple, 328 orange and 614 yellow.

years.h: Patrick Flynn of Have Heart guests on Up River
years.p: The Most is Revelation REV 141, produced by Jim Siegel. Have Heart is the band whose reunion Down to Nothing plays twelve years later.

years.h: Spector writes Unbreakable songs on a European tour
years.p: Revelation REV 146 comes in 330 white and 330 red copies. Daniel Spector writes the new material on that year's European tour.

years.big: "Terror is professional. DTN is goofy chaos vacation."
years.h: Wood takes the bass spot in Terror
years.p: Wood tells DxR that Terror was one of his favorite bands, so it was hard to say no when they asked him in late spring 2008.
years.xp: Wood had toured with Terror before joining. He says Terror is serious because it is his job, and

eras.title: Terror is the job
eras.text: With Wood on the road with Terror, Down to Nothing played rarely. They were technically still under contract to Revelation, but the next record came out on Reaper.

years.cap: Wood working the crowd at Arena, Richmond, September 2009
years.h: Terror is Wood's job, so All My Sons comes out on Reaper
years.p: The 7" gets a July 4 release show and a Sound and Fury set. Down to Nothing hadn't played since January.
years.xp:
Wood told Dying Scene: "Terror is my job. We're on the road almost 300 days a year."

The band was technically still under contract to Revelation. Wood says that since they don't tour much and Revelation "isn't much of a label anymore," the label left the decision to them.

Spector wrote the songs and sent them over. "We changed a few things," Wood says.

years.h: Live at Sound and Fury, July 24, 2010
yt: Live at Sound and Fury, July 24, 2010

eras.title: Love letters to the James River
eras.text: Five years after Unbreakable, the band made a record about Richmond itself: Belle Isle, Pipeline, Shafer Court, Monroe Park. Spector wrote it between shifts as an emergency medicine resident.

years.cap: Down to Nothing crowd on the Life on the James tour, September 2013
years.h: Greetings From Richmond Virginia 7" arrives as REV 152
years.p: The first pressing is 520 yellow, 526 white and 550 black.

years.cap: Life on the James record release show, Kingdom, Richmond, September 21, 2013
q: Every band from out of town felt like they had a home in Richmond.
years.h: Fans drive up from Florida to stand on Belle Isle
years.p: Daniel Spector writes all the music for Life on the James (REV 153) while working as an emergency medicine resident at VCU. The songs name Belle Isle, Pipeline, Shafer Court and Monroe Park.
years.xp:
RVA Mag put the band in a line with [[Avail|d67ff511-57b8-4d02-94d3-6c6a331c2ae4]], whose Dixie and Over the James also mapped the city. Spector recalled that in the late 90s "you were guaranteed to see a fight, at least one or two every show."

By 2013 Down to Nothing were selling out Kingdom. Wood: "It still hasn't sunk in that we've sold out a venue in Richmond."

Wood calls it his favorite Down to Nothing record.

years.cap: Down to Nothing, Wood in the crowd, February 2015
years.h: Scott Vogel slips a disc, and Wood sings for Terror
years.p: Terror vocalist [[Scott Vogel|4ab1b4fb-f2fe-458c-a496-0de55c7bf3cb]] hurts his back on the summer 2015 US tour. David Wood takes the mic for the last shows and the European run.
years.xp: Wood tells DxR that Vogel slipped the disc on the third-to-last show of the US tour. Wood sang the final two dates, then covered the entire six-week European tour.

years.cap: Down to Nothing at Sound & Fury, The Regent, Los Angeles, 2016
years.src: Bandcamp: Live! On The James · Revelation Records
years.h: Live! On the James arrives the year Wood leaves Terror
years.p: Revelation REV 165, January 20. Seventeen songs live, opening on Life on the James; the first pressing is 1,096 gold and 324 pink.

years.h: The last Down to Nothing show is Have Heart's reunion
years.p: Down to Nothing's final appearance is at [[Have Heart|e519e012-e1a3-4592-b3f6-5a16227ab654]]'s reunion shows at the Worcester Palladium in Massachusetts. After that the band goes inactive.
